title: Swift 1.5 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 on two Sparks
evidence_scope: Revision 3ff0520224f264a2d0ac4ab56ece8f2f13aadb38 of ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 with the qwen38-flash-next-tp2 settings for the same Qwen4Exp architecture, except where this checkpoint's format differs: ModelOpt NVFP4 routed experts (--quantization modelopt_fp4), the 95.4 GiB BF16 PLE n-gram table read from the checkpoint files with io_uring (VLLM_PLE_TABLE_MEMORY=disk), and BF16 MTP draft experts on vLLM's unquantized MoE kernel, on installer image dev-20260927-h2dstaging-cuda1342-nccl2323-status031: sparkring install downloaded the checkpoint and started the model on one Spark pair, the functional checks (counting, arithmetic, code, tool calls, image, thinking) and a 256-request correctness screen passed, and a temperature-1.0 throughput matrix was measured (performance/records/images/dev-20260927-h2dstaging-swift15-qwen38-tp2-20260927.md); single-run timing; not serving-qualified. This profile runs image dev-20260927-b12xcache-cuda1342-nccl2323-status032, which is dev-20260927-h2dstaging-cuda1342-nccl2323-status031 with a B12X selection-cache correction, so starts on several Sparks reuse the kernel tuning the ranks have already agreed on, and runtime-status 0.3.2, whose dashboard shows the served model name; the evidence above was measured on dev-20260927-h2dstaging-cuda1342-nccl2323-status031.
